newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends down v dlr, forward premia harden.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends down v dlr, forward premia harden.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened to end Tuesday at 35.72/73 against the day's opening quotes of 35.70/71, dealers said.
Dealers said the rupee traded on Tuesday at a low of 35.735 per dollar and a high of 35.69.
They said the rupee slipped later in the day on short-covering by banks and dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

"Basically the market is still range-bound," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Some banks were short in the morning. As they covered their posiitons and the RBI came in to buy dollars, the rupee slipped."
"Otherwise demand from importers is still not there."
Dealers said the RBI bought dollars at 35.70 and 35.71 levels. While the amount could not be quantified, one dealer said the RBI bought in "good" quantities.
Premia on forward dollars firmed up on paying pressure by some financial institutions, dealers said.

"The sentiment in forwards is still soft with prospects for domestic liquidity looking good," said a dealer. "Premia went up slightly today because a couple of financial institutions were paying (booking forward)."
The premia on six-month dollars ended Tuesday at an annualised 8.45 percent against Monday's close of 8.06 percent, dealers said.
